blueprints.name: B2 综合理解（新闻/论述，约 320 词）
C1 学术理解（研究/论文，约 300 词）

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why coffee machines frequently break down
The debate over and development of the right to repair
How manufacturers produce longer-lasting batteries
Differences between repair shops across countries

questions.q: According to supporters, which is a benefit of repairability?
options: It makes devices cheaper to manufacture
It adds more repair instructions to every manual
It reduces electronic waste and saves consumers money
It removes the need for product warranties

questions.q: Which point is NOT raised by manufacturers as a concern?
options: An untrained repair attempt may cause fires or injuries
Public manuals could let competitors copy designs cheaply
Restricting firmware access protects security features
Repaired devices consume significantly more electricity

questions.q: France's repairability score is mentioned as an example of what?
options: A law trying to balance consumers' and manufacturers' interests
A penalty applied to makers of unsafe products
Why spare parts must be kept for seven years
How consumers can open and fix machines by themselves

questions.q: According to the passage, why was the number 42 route restored?
options: It was extended to reach the central hospital
Night-shift workers had no reliable late-night alternative
Ride-hailing apps had become unsafe at night
Students demanded cheaper monthly ticketing

questions.q: What did the simple "arithmetic" of cutting night buses hide?
options: That night operating costs were steadily falling
That metro carriages were overcrowded at midnight
An inequity between office workers and night-shift workers
The real number of tourists taking taxis

questions.q: How do several cities fund their night services?
options: A small levy on late-opening bars and clubs
Higher prices on monthly travel passes
Fines collected from drunk drivers
Direct grants from local hospitals

questions.q: What point does the cleaner make about the bus?
options: It is faster than the first metro service
It removes two unpaid hours from her working day
It lets her eat dinner before her shift
It will make headlines like a new metro line

questions.q: Why did written tests largely replace oral examinations?
options: They were cheaper to grade and easier to standardise
Students did poorly in doctoral defences
Universities banned follow-up questions
Language classes asked for more writing

questions.q: Why has generative artificial intelligence revived oral exams?
options: AI tools cannot write polished essays quickly
A take-home paper no longer proves its author understands the work
Students prefer being questioned by software
AI can grade spoken answers more fairly than humans

questions.q: Which advantage of oral exams do early reports describe?
options: They are easy to fake with elegant phrasing
They reward genuine understanding and train speaking under pressure
One examiner can grade hundreds of students a day
Nervous speakers consistently earn higher marks

questions.q: What fairness concern about oral exams is raised?
options: Written scripts take less time to grade
A nervous speaker or unfamiliar accent may bias results
Marking criteria cannot be released in advance
Whiteboard problems favour doctoral students

questions.q: What does the growing body of research suggest about green space?
options: It is a luxury cities can afford only in good times
Its absence carries measurable health costs
It mainly benefits the wealthiest residents
It has no measurable effect on stress

questions.q: What is the most consistent mental-health finding?
options: Only unemployed residents reported lower stress
Depression diagnoses increased near renovated parks
People near parks report less stress even after controlling for income
Social contact alone explains every measured benefit

questions.q: How do critics respond to the heart-disease findings?
options: They are correlational, since wealthier areas have both parks and healthcare
Tree cover directly causes heart disease
Heat waves have no connection to mortality
Vegetation worsens local wind patterns

questions.q: What does "green gentrification" refer to?
options: New parks tending to lower nearby property values
New parks pushing out the residents who most needed the benefits
Engineering problems that stop parks being built
Political questions that have no effect on access

questions.q: What central question does the study examine?
options: Whether optimal spacing intervals differ by learner proficiency
Why pseudo-words are easier to learn than real words
How Chinese-speaking learners teach vocabulary
Whether massed practice beats all schedules at one week

questions.q: What did the results show?
options: The 3-day interval worked best for B1 learners, the 7-day for C1 learners
Massed conditions outperformed spaced conditions at four weeks
B1 and C1 learners performed identically in every condition
The 7-day condition was best for both proficiency groups

questions.q: Why did the researchers use pseudo-words?
options: To make the task easier for B1 learners
To control for learners' prior exposure to the items
To reduce the number of participants required
To avoid pre-registering the analysis plan

questions.q: What practical implication is suggested for scheduling software?
options: Uniform default intervals may be sub-optimal for advanced learners
Software should rely only on massed study sessions
Memory models predict no spacing effect at all
Advanced learners should be given shorter intervals than beginners

questions.q: What is the study's main finding?
options: The brightest streets were 0.6–1.1 °C warmer at 02:00
Lighting has no association with night temperature
Daytime maxima drive most heat-related mortality
Vegetation raises nighttime air temperatures

questions.q: Which two mechanisms do the authors propose?
options: Luminaires release heat and bright surfaces delay radiative cooling
Traffic density raises the efficiency of luminaires
Buildings block satellite signals at night
Full-cutoff fixtures trap cool air at street level

questions.q: What do the results suggest for policy?
options: After-midnight dimming achieved cooling with no measured rise in crime
Curfews caused a sharp increase in accidents
Cities should raise illumination above 80 lux
Dimming reliably increased crime records

questions.q: Which limitation is acknowledged?
options: The cities share one climate zone and residual confounding remains
Satellite data measured indoor temperatures directly
Hot-arid cities had already been fully replicated
Energy records showed lighting consumed no power
